method_card.title: My Town and Local Area
method_card.content:
This lesson covers describing your town, what there is to do and where things are located, using es gibt, man kann, and two-way prepositions.

GermanEnglish
die Stadt (ü-e)town / city
das Dorf (ü-er)village
der Vorort (-e)suburb
das Stadtzentrumtown centre
das Einkaufszentrumshopping centre
das Schwimmbad (ä-er)swimming pool
die Bibliothek (-en)library
das Rathaus (ä-er)town hall
der Markt (ä-e)market
lebhaftlively
langweiligboring
ruhigquiet / peaceful
sichersafe
man kann + infinitiveyou can / one can
(Higher) der Stadtrandoutskirts (of town)

Grammar focus 1 — es gibt + accusative: es gibt means 'there is / there are' and takes the accusative case. Masculine indefinite article ein becomes einen: Es gibt einen Park. Feminine stays eine: Es gibt eine Bibliothek. Neuter stays ein: Es gibt ein Kino.

Grammar focus 2 — man kann + infinitive: man (one / you) takes the er/sie/es verb form. Modal kann sits at position 2; the second verb goes to the end as an infinitive: Man kann im Park spazieren gehen. (You can go for a walk in the park.)

Grammar focus 3 — two-way prepositions (location = dative): in, an, auf, über, unter, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen take the dative when describing where something is (Wo?): im Stadtzentrum (in dem → im), neben dem Park, auf dem Markt. They take the accusative for movement into a place (Wohin?): Ich gehe in die Bibliothek.

Model: Ich wohne in einer kleinen Stadt im Nordwesten. Es gibt einen Park, ein Kino und viele Geschäfte. Man kann einkaufen gehen und im Schwimmbad schwimmen. Die Stadt ist ruhig, aber manchmal langweilig. (I live in a small town in the north-west. There is a park, a cinema and many shops. You can go shopping and swim at the swimming pool. The town is peaceful, but sometimes boring.)
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for places in town, including each noun's gender (der/die/das)
Master es gibt + accusative — remember einen for masculine nouns
Practise man kann + infinitive at the end of the clause
Use two-way prepositions with dative for location: im, am, auf dem, neben dem
Build full sentences combining es gibt, man kann, and dative prepositions with capital nouns

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — town and local area appears across all papers

worked_examples.question: What does 'In meiner Stadt kann man viel machen' mean?

steps.label: Identify key words
steps.content: In meiner Stadt = in my town. kann man = you can / one can.

steps.label: Translate the rest
steps.content: viel machen = do a lot. Notice the infinitive machen sits at the end.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: In my town you can do a lot.

worked_examples.question: Why is it 'es gibt einen Park' but 'es gibt ein Kino'?

steps.label: The rule
steps.content: es gibt (there is / there are) takes the accusative case — the noun is the direct object.

steps.label: Apply the case
steps.content: der Park is masculine. In the accusative, masculine ein becomes einen. das Kino is neuter — neuter accusative stays ein. Feminine die Bibliothek → accusative stays eine.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Masculine nouns add -en in the accusative after es gibt. Feminine and neuter do not change: Es gibt einen Park, eine Bibliothek, ein Kino.

worked_examples.question: Translate: 'The town hall is behind the market, next to the bank.' How do the two-way prepositions work here?

steps.label: Choose the case
steps.content: The sentence describes location (Wo? — where is it?), so both prepositions take the dative. der Markt → dative dem Markt. die Bank → dative der Bank.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Das Rathaus ist hinter dem Markt, neben der Bank.

bronze.question: Match the German places to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct form after es gibt

gaps.correct_explain: einen is correct. es gibt takes the accusative. der Park is masculine — accusative masculine indefinite article = einen.

wrong.ein: ein is the masculine nominative or neuter form. After es gibt, masculine nouns need the accusative: einen.
wrong.der: der is the nominative definite article, not the indefinite accusative. Use einen.

gaps.correct_explain: ein is correct. das Kino is neuter — neuter accusative indefinite article stays ein.

wrong.einen: einen is masculine accusative. das Kino is neuter — neuter accusative stays ein.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence using man kann

gaps.correct_explain: kann is the er/sie/es form of können. man always takes the er/sie/es form.

wrong.können: können is the infinitive or wir/sie form. With man, use the er/sie/es form: kann.

gaps.rule: Infinitive at end with modal verb
gaps.correct_explain: gehen is the infinitive, placed at the end of the clause after the modal verb.

wrong.geht: geht is a conjugated form. After a modal verb, use the infinitive at the end.

bronze.question: What does 'Ich finde meine Stadt langweilig, weil es nichts für junge Leute gibt' mean?
options: I find my town boring because there is nothing for young people
I find my town exciting because there is a lot for young people
I think my town is too big for young people
Young people find my town interesting

bronze.question: What does 'Die Stadt ist größer als das Dorf' mean?
options: The city is bigger than the village
The city is as big as the village
The village is bigger than the city
The city is the biggest in the village

bronze.source_text: Ich wohne in einer kleinen Stadt. Es gibt einen Park und viele Geschäfte.
model_answers: I live in a small town. There is a park and many shops.
hints: Es gibt = there is / there are

bronze.audio_text: Ich wohne in einer kleinen Stadt.
bronze.correct_text: Ich wohne in einer kleinen Stadt.
bronze.translation: I live in a small town.

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: The village is **quieter** than the city, but the city has **better** transport connections.
sentence_parts: als die Stadt, aber die Stadt hat

wrong.ruhig: ruhig is the base form. For comparison with als (than), add -er: ruhiger.

gaps.rule: Comparative — irregular (gut → besser) + adjective ending before plural noun
gaps.correct_explain: bessere = better. gut → besser is irregular. Before the plural noun Verkehrsverbindungen, the comparative takes the adjective ending -e.

wrong.besser: besser needs an adjective ending before the noun. Before plural nominative nouns, add -e: bessere.
wrong.guter: guter uses the base form — you need the comparative: gut → besser.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Die Stadt ist groß als das Dorf.
silver.explanation: For comparisons with als (than), you need the comparative form. groß → größer (add -er + umlaut). Without the -er ending, the comparison makes no grammatical sense.
silver.translation: The city is bigger than the village.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: I like living here because there is a lot to do.

distractor_labels.gerne: gern and gerne are both correct German, but gern is already in the correct order — using both creates a duplicate.

silver.source_text: There is too much traffic and not enough for young people. The buses don't run often enough.
model_answers: Es gibt zu viel Verkehr und nicht genug für junge Leute. Die Busse fahren nicht oft genug.
silver.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a translation from English to German. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Check: es gibt + accusative (zu viel Verkehr — mass noun, no article change needed), negation nicht genug, die Busse fahren nicht (verb position). Accept valid alternatives. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

silver.question: Listen and type what you hear
silver.audio_text: Man kann im Park spazieren gehen und einkaufen gehen.
silver.correct_text: Man kann im Park spazieren gehen und einkaufen gehen.
silver.translation: You can go for a walk in the park and go shopping.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: I would prefer to live in a big city because there is more to do. Country life is healthier but more boring, and the buses don't run often enough.
model_answers: Ich möchte lieber in einer Großstadt wohnen, weil es mehr zu tun gibt. Das Landleben ist gesünder aber langweiliger, und die Busse fahren nicht oft genug.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a Gold-tier translation. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Check: möchte lieber + infinitive at end, dative after in (in einer Großstadt), weil + verb-final (gibt), comparatives gesünder and langweiliger (both take -er, gesünder adds umlaut), negation nicht oft genug. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: It annoys me that there is no train station.

distractor_labels.mir: wrong pronoun — nerven takes the accusative: es nervt mich (not mir, which is dative).
distractor_labels.kein: wrong case — es gibt takes the accusative. Bahnhof is masculine: kein → keinen.
distractor_labels.keine: wrong gender — der Bahnhof is masculine, so use keinen not keine (feminine).

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are visiting a tourist information office in a German town. The member of staff speaks to you.

bullets.prompt: Greet the staff member and say you are looking for the town centre.
bullets.model_answer: Guten Tag! Ich suche das Stadtzentrum. Können Sie mir helfen?
bullets.note: polite greeting + Ich suche + accusative (das Stadtzentrum) + Können Sie...? (Sie register)

bullets.prompt: Ask what there is to do in the town.
bullets.model_answer: Was kann man in der Stadt machen? Gibt es ein Kino oder ein Museum?
bullets.note: man kann (general) + question with Gibt es + accusative

bullets.prompt: Say you would like to go to the market and ask what time it opens.
bullets.model_answer: Ich möchte zum Markt gehen. Um wie viel Uhr öffnet er?
bullets.note: ich möchte + infinitive at end, zum (zu + dem, dative contraction for der Markt), opening-hours question

bullets.prompt: Say you will come back tomorrow with your family.
bullets.model_answer: Ich werde morgen mit meiner Familie wiederkommen.
bullets.note: future: werden + infinitive at end, mit + dative (meiner Familie — dative feminine)

gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a role play set in a tourist information office. All prompts are in a formal Sie-register context. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did they communicate the required information? (2) Is the German grammatically accurate? Check: Sie register, accusative after suche/gibt es, dative after in/zum/mit, werden + infinitive at end. Award marks out of 10 total. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"Per-bullet feedback","improvement":"Key grammar point to revise"}

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German comparing town and country life. Include: what your area is like, what you can do there, a comparison with another type of area, and where you would like to live in the future.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about town and local area. Mark on: Communication (did they address all four points?), Range of language (es gibt + accusative, man kann + infinitive, comparatives with -er + als, möchte/würde + infinitive, weil + verb-final), Accuracy (dative after in/neben/auf etc., correct comparative forms with umlauts like größer/ruhiger, noun capitalisation). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Ich wohne gern hier, weil es viel zu tun gibt, aber ich möchte lieber in einer Großstadt wohnen.
gold.correct_text: Ich wohne gern hier, weil es viel zu tun gibt, aber ich möchte lieber in einer Großstadt wohnen.
gold.translation: I like living here because there is a lot to do, but I would prefer to live in a big city.

gold.source_text: If I were rich, I would live by the sea in a big house. My dream town would be lively and modern.
model_answers: Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich am Meer in einem großen Haus wohnen. Meine Traumstadt wäre lebhaft und modern.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a Higher-tier translation testing Konjunktiv II. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Tests: Konjunktiv II (wäre, würde + infinitive at end), wenn + verb-final (wäre), dative after in (in einem großen Haus — adjective ending after indefinite article: gemischte Deklination, neuter dative: -em), am Meer (an + dem = am, dative). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional specific correction"}
